title: Unemployment Insurance Appeals Language Services: Interpreter Reset Lead for Reopened Hearings
content:
In Unemployment Insurance Appeals, when a dismissed appeal is reopened and its hearing set again, the reopened-setting interpreter lead is read from the latest interpreter request on the appeal — the request with the most recent request date.

**Standard.** The reopened-setting interpreter lead is the sign-language reset lead days when the latest interpreter request on the appeal is for American Sign Language, the contract-interpreter reset lead days when the latest interpreter request on the appeal is for a language other than American Sign Language and Spanish, and zero days when the latest interpreter request is for Spanish or no interpreter is requested. The reopened hearing date found from the reopened-setting clock and the reopened-setting window is moved later by this lead before the notice minimum and the weekend rule are applied.

| Latest interpreter request on the appeal | Reopened-setting interpreter lead |
|---|---|
| American Sign Language | 10 calendar days (sign-language reset lead) |
| a language other than American Sign Language and Spanish | 7 calendar days (contract-interpreter reset lead) |
| Spanish | 0 days |
| none | 0 days |

## Points of judgement

- Only the latest request counts; an earlier request for another language on the same appeal does not.
- The lead is in calendar days.

*Hypothetical cases:* requests for Polish (2 March) and then American Sign Language (12 March) — 10 days; American Sign Language (2 March) and then Spanish (12 March) — 0 days; a single request for Arabic — 7 days.
